title: Settling or steady noise? Within-recording firing-rate trends of untreated human iPSC and rat wells (REAL data, Kapucu 2022)
status: registered before any windowed (sub-half) feature was computed for any well
origin: D32 (report section 36) found human iPSC firing rate about twice as noisy as rat between the two halves of one untreated recording, and noted that human wells fall more within the recording, so part of the split-half spread may be uneven settling rather than steady noise; no test separated the two
seen_before_registration: everything in hpsc_split_half (D32): per-well split-half changes, their SDs and R per feature, the usable wells (24 human, 38 rat on the 48-well baselines), the mean firing-rate change (human -0.32, rat -0.17 log2), the figure of per-well changes, and the firing-rate overlap check
no firing rate or other feature of any window shorter than half a recording, for any well
data: the D32 primary pool only: hPSC_MEA3Baseline_DIV29 and Rat_MEA2Baseline_DIV22 (48-well, 30-min untreated baselines), the wells D32 judged usable

method.windows: each recording cut into 6 consecutive windows of equal length (5 min for these 30-min recordings); window k = 0..5
method.electrodes: per well, the electrodes active over the whole recording (the extractor's active rule at defaults); the same set in every window, so a changing electrode set cannot move the rate
method.rate: r_k = mean over those electrodes of spikes in window k / window length; y_k = log2(max(r_k, 1 / (n_electrodes x window length)))
method.trend: per well, ordinary least squares of y_k on (k - 2.5): slope b (log2 per window) and residual SD s (ddof 2)
method.decomposition: per well, the split-half change is d = mean(y_3..5) - mean(y_0..2); its trend part is d_trend = 3b; its residual part is d - d_trend
method.bootstrap: 2,000 resamples of wells within each species, seed 20261028

T1_human_settling_more_uneven.statement: human wells settle more unevenly: the spread of the within-recording slope across wells is larger in human than in rat wells
T1_human_settling_more_uneven.test: pass if the 95% interval of SD(b)_human / SD(b)_rat lies above 1; fail otherwise

T2_human_steady_noise_larger.statement: human wells are also noisier around their own trend
T2_human_steady_noise_larger.test: pass if the 95% interval of median(s)_human / median(s)_rat lies above 1; fail otherwise

T3_settling_carries_the_human_spread.statement: in human wells, the trend carries most of the split-half spread
T3_settling_carries_the_human_spread.test: pass if var(d_trend) / var(d) over human wells is at least 0.5 (point estimate); fail otherwise; the same share for rat wells is reported

uninterpretable: every prediction is uninterpretable if fewer than 10 wells per species have a defined rate in all six windows

reported_not_tested.wells_needed: the D32 wells-needed lower bound recomputed from the residual part alone (what remains if each well's own trend were removed, for example by a longer settling period before dosing), stated as illustrative
reported_not_tested.per_window: the median rate per window per species, as a settling curve

assumption_check.assumption: a straight line describes the within-recording trend well enough that its slope means settling
assumption_check.check: per well, add a quadratic term and report the share of wells in which it lowers the residual SD by more than a third; if that share exceeds one half in either species, the report says the trend is not linear and reads T1 and T3 with that caveat

reporting: all three predictions reported with values whatever the outcome
